attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation does not show that every small arbitrary circuit for H_N yields such a quotient sketch. It is an upper-bound falsifier, not a lower-bound certificate.
steps: Normalize each generated multiset by deleting pairs with equal SAT-preserving quotient class; the remaining parity-incidence vector is a_N(x).
For an affine cell, fix a basis b_{i,1},...,b_{i,r_i} and hardwire the bits <lambda_N,b_{i,l}> plus the affine offset bit; compute the coordinate decoder and XOR the selected constants.
For a codebook cell, hardwire p_{i,t}=<lambda_N,v_{i,t}> for every transcript value t in [R_i]; compute t_i(x) and evaluate a table circuit of size O(R_i log R_i).
Use the cheaper implementation on each cell, multiplex by the cell locator, and patch each of the E uncovered seeds by an equality test on the N-bit input.
The resulting circuit size is O(S+sum_i min{r_i,R_i log R_i}+EN), so any sketch below N^{1+epsilon} contradicts the desired source lower bound.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The main hard step remains a direct N^{1+epsilon} lower bound for H_N or a nonrelativizing extraction theorem. The valid target bridge alone cannot separate P from NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-Magnification Bridge Realization: XOR quotient codebook gate

assumptions: L=(log N)^d for a fixed d>1, M=N^q, and q,rho<1+epsilon.
The generator outputs formulas and parity positions by circuits of size at most N^rho.
The quotient relation on generated formulas is SAT-preserving, so every quotient class has a well-defined label lambda_N(u)=SAT(u).
A sketch consists of a cell locator, optional affine coordinate decoders, optional exact codebook transcripts, and an error set of at most E seeds.
definitions: source object: the generated XOR carrier H_N on N-bit seeds, using M=N^q generated SAT instances of length L=(log N)^d and normalized quotient-incidence vector a_N(x) in F_2^{Q_N}.

target object: nonuniform circuits for SAT on length-L formulas, with the intended target consequence SAT notin SIZE(n^c) for every fixed c, hence SAT notin P/poly if the source lower bound holds for unbounded N.
controlled interface: substitute a hypothesized SAT circuit for each generated query, compute the generator and parity incidence, and charge only N^rho+N^q L^c+lower-order wiring.

target-preserving condition: the quotient must preserve SAT labels and only cancel even multiplicities; source-side transcript advice may be used as an upper-bound falsifier but must not be smuggled into the target substitution bridge.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find S+sum_i min{r_i,R_i log R_i}+EN<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} for the actual quotient-incidence map; then the proposed H_N lower bound is invalid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route bridge and source-audit lemma: it preserves the known XOR target transfer while adding a stronger nonuniform-leakage falsifier for the source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Quotient codebook-or-rank sketch upper bound for generated XOR carriers. Let H_N(x)=xor_{j<=M} SAT(phi_{N,j}(x)) with M=N^q, formula length L=(log N)^d, and generator size N^rho. After odd-multiplicity cancellation in a SAT-preserving quotient Q_N, write H_N(x)=<lambda_N,a_N(x)> over F_2. If all but E inputs are covered by cells whose quotient-incidence vectors have either affine coordinate dimension r_i or exact transcript codebook size R_i, with total locator/decoder circuit size S, then C(H_N)<=O(S+sum_i min{r_i,R_i log R_i}+EN). Hence any N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound must rule out all subthreshold quotient codebook-or-rank sketches; such a sketch is a concrete falsifier, not merely weak evidence.

assumptions: The cell recognizer and transcript or coordinate maps are nonuniform circuits included in S.
The quotient classes have fixed SAT labels at length N, so table bits are legal nonuniform advice for an upper bound on H_N.
The sketch is exact outside an explicitly patchable error set.
definitions: affine leakage: a cell has a computable coordinate map into an r-dimensional affine subspace of F_2^{Q_N}.
codebook leakage: a cell has a computable transcript selecting one of R exact quotient-incidence vectors.
hardwired parity table: for each codeword v, store the single bit <lambda_N,v>, requiring no SAT solver on new inputs.
threshold charge: the usable sketch cost is the smaller of the rank charge and the transcript-table charge on each cell.

equations.label: cell-cost
equations.valid_when: Applies when both an affine decoder and an exact transcript decoder are available on the same cell.

equations.label: source-obligation
equations.valid_when: Requires using the sketch family as an upper-bound audit for the same source circuit model as C(H_N).

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A nonlinear low-cardinality transcript partition defeats rank-only audits; a low-rank span defeats codebook-only audits.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents promotion of high rank or high entropy alone as lower-bound evidence for the XOR carrier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite codebook leakage is independent of affine-rank leakage. A family of quotient-incidence vectors may have affine rank N^{1+epsilon} but only N^alpha transcript values on each efficiently recognized cell, or may have huge transcript image but affine rank N^alpha. In either case alpha<1+epsilon gives a valid source upper-bound falsifier after hardwiring either cell parities or basis parities.

assumptions: No unproved normal form converts arbitrary circuits for H_N into local quotient sketches.
The SAT predicate is the real Boolean satisfiability language, not an arbitrary oracle label vector.
The intended source lower bound is against general nonuniform Boolean circuits.
definitions: relativizing part: the substitution SAT in SIZE(n^c) => C(H_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} works for any oracle interpretation of SAT labels.
nonrelativizing needed part: a theorem forcing arbitrary small H_N circuits to expose quotient codebook-or-rank structure for the real SAT predicate.
natural-proof risk: a largeness argument saying most label vectors lambda make H_N hard would not isolate real SAT and would collide with pseudorandom-function barriers.
scope limitation: the present lemma gives upper-bound falsifiers only; it is not a proof of P != NP.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Barrier audit for the XOR quotient route. The target substitution bridge is relativizing and easy, but any positive source lower bound for H_N against arbitrary circuits cannot be certified merely by quotient entropy, affine rank, random-label behavior, or separator hardness. A valid proof must either lower-bound H_N directly or give a nonrelativizing extraction theorem from small H_N circuits to subthreshold quotient sketches.

Rank, transcript image, parity cancellation, and patchable errors form a finite quantitative falsifier suite for candidate XOR generators.

falsifiers: Subthreshold quotient codebook sketch: S+sum_i R_i log R_i+EN<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} makes H_N easy by hardwired parity values.
Low affine rank after SAT-preserving quotient: S+sum_i r_i+EN<N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} makes H_N easy by hardwired basis parities.
Symmetry-pair cancellation: most generated SAT instances cancel modulo 2 inside Q_N, causing constant or low-transcript carriers despite high raw formula entropy.
Target threshold collapse: max{rho,q}>=1+epsilon invalidates the magnification implication even if the source lower bound is true.
Model mismatch falsifier: quotienting formulas by a relation that is not SAT-preserving breaks the identity H_N=<lambda_N,a_N>.
Nonuniform leakage through a short transcript table may decide H_N without computing SAT on any new formula.
Natural-proof falsifier: a proof using only random-label hardness of lambda_N would not identify real SAT and is not valid route evidence under standard pseudorandomness barriers.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No size-preserving, padding-stable compiler from Boolean SIZE(m^c) deciders for SAT_m to low-support depth-4 circuits computing MLE(SAT_m) within the same SPD threshold.
steps: Start with P_m=MLE(SAT_m) over F and choose k,l,D,t,S=m^c after a proposed depth-reduction interface.
Assume a lower bound SPD_{k,l}^F(P_m)>S binom(D,k) binom(m,l+kt).
By the low-support depth-4 upper bound, conclude P_m is not computed by SigmaPiSigmaPi_F(S,D,t); this is a valid restricted arithmetic consequence.
Try to convert SAT in P, witnessed by Boolean circuits of size m^c, into such a depth-4 circuit for P_m.

Gate arithmetization gives a small arithmetic circuit agreeing with SAT on the Boolean cube, but it need not compute MLE(SAT_m), may have degree 2^{m^c}, and depth reduction can destroy the D,t threshold.
Determinant supplies the sanity check: strong depth-4 arithmetic lower bounds can hold for a polynomial-time computable family.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves only a restricted arithmetic lower bound. It does not exclude polynomial-time Boolean algorithms, and its proof object may be algebraically natural without addressing the Boolean target.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier audit for shifted-partial-derivative arithmetic lower-bound routes

assumptions: F is fixed before the lower-bound statement and is not chosen from the input.
The upper-bound theorem for SigmaPiSigmaPi_F(S,D,t) is invoked with explicit k,l,D,t.
The source polynomial is given explicitly enough that the SPD witness is not merely a nonuniform truth-table artifact.
Boolean arithmetization by gate replacement is allowed only as cube agreement, not as computation of the unique multilinear extension.
definitions: source object: a polynomial family P_m over a fixed field F, typically the multilinear extension MLE(SAT_m) or an algebraic benchmark such as Det_n.
target object: low-support homogeneous depth-4 arithmetic circuits SigmaPiSigmaPi_F(S,D,t) of size S, formal product fan-in D, and bottom support at most t.
controlled interface: compare SPD_{k,l}^F(P_m) with the standard upper bound U_{k,l}(m,S,D,t) for the named arithmetic model.

target-preserving condition: for P-vs-NP use, the polynomial must be the canonical SAT truth-table extension and Boolean size m^c must imply a circuit inside the same SigmaPiSigmaPi_F(S,D,t) threshold after padding and multilinearization.
SPD_{k,l} is the dimension of shifted k-th partial derivatives after multilinear projection.
The route is algebraic and may be algebraically natural; this is harmless for restricted arithmetic lower bounds but invalid as a Boolean lower-bound transfer without the missing compiler.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The argument does not rule out genuinely non-black-box proof systems or algebraic commitments that bind all N row bits without replayable T-query transcripts; those mechanisms must be named and audited for naturalness, algebrization, and advice leakage.
steps: Fix a deterministic accepting computation of V^T(pi) and let Q be the adaptive set of row positions queried on that computation.
Define A_Q to agree with T on Q and to be zero outside Q. A_Q is computed by an OR of equality tests for the queried positive positions, so size(A_Q)=O(|Q|m).
Run V^{A_Q}(pi). Every adaptive query receives the same answer as in the original transcript, hence the verifier follows the same path and accepts.
If |Q|m=o(2^{epsilon m}), then A_Q is an accepted row with unrestricted circuits below the claimed MCSP threshold.
Therefore a black-box relation claiming universal anti-ball soundness must either read Omega(2^{epsilon m}/m) row bits or use a separately specified non-black-box binding mechanism.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a route-level falsifier and threshold lemma. It gives no construction of a valid low-D anti-ball carrier and therefore gives no direct progress on the main P != NP conjecture.

assumptions: V has no nonuniform advice and accesses the row T only by adaptive bit queries; proof bits may be arbitrary but cannot change T-query answers.
The source relation claims universal soundness: every accepted pair (T,pi) is an MCSP no-side row at threshold 2^{epsilon m}.
The target extraction uses exact row hardness; existential hard rows require the earlier multiplexing repair and do not license a black-box soundness claim.
definitions: source object: black-box symbolic anti-ball verifier V^T(pi) for T in {0,1}^{2^m}, with transcript query set Q and claimed soundness against circuits of size 2^{epsilon m}.
target object: an E-uniform low-D MCSP carrier whose accepted hard rows multiplex to an E truth-table lower bound.
controlled interface: accepted certificate plus universal soundness -> MCSP no-side row -> low-D multiplexing -> all-length E circuit lower bound.
target-preserving condition: no advice, E-canonical row selection, kappa-dense lengths, distinct-image entropy D, and transcript binding strong enough to avoid easy zero-fill replays.
q_V(m,pi) is the number of T-bit queries made on the accepting transcript after fixing the deterministic verifier and certificate.
A_Q is the table agreeing with T on queried positions Q and equal to 0 outside Q.

equations.label: transcript_soundness_load
equations.valid_when: Valid for black-box universal-sound verifiers whose acceptance can be replayed after changing all unread truth-table bits.

equations.label: short_black_box_collapse
equations.valid_when: Applies when the verifier reads only polynomially many row bits from a linear-size symbolic certificate.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Source-side falsifier and threshold repair. It rules out sparse black-box proof certificates while preserving the conditional carrier-to-E extraction if a non-black-box binding source is supplied.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Transcript-load no-go for black-box symbolic anti-ball certificates: if a deterministic verifier V^T(pi) accepts after reading q truth-table bits and soundness requires every accepted T to have circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m}, then q=Omega(2^{epsilon m}/m). Otherwise the same transcript accepts a zero-filled table of size O(qm), a direct falsifier for the source relation.

assumptions: S=2^{epsilon m}, R=2^{rho m}, and T has length N=2^m.
The proof-system verifier is uniform and sound for all formulas in the encoded Near family.
The construction either reads or binds enough T-bits to avoid the transcript-load falsifier from cycle56.lemma.black_box_transcript_load.
definitions: Near_{m,S,R}(T) asserts that some circuit C of size at most S disagrees with T on at most R inputs.
The source proof object is a pair (T,pi) where pi is accepted by a named sound proof-system verifier for the unrolled Near formula.
The target row object is T, not the proof pi; proof length affects explicitness but not the circuit lower-bound threshold once verification is E-time.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Names a concrete proof-complexity source model for symbolic anti-ball certificates and exposes the verifier-binding obligation.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A sound Cook-Reckhow proof of UNSAT(Near_{m,S,R}(T)) is a valid symbolic anti-ball certificate, provided the formula generation is E-uniform from the row stream and the proof system has no advice. The bridge is conditional source progress, not a proof of P != NP.

assumptions: Low-D distinct-image unranking is E-canonical and advice-free.
The row-length set is kappa-dense after padding.
The anti-ball proof is sound for the stated center exponent, not just for a syntactic subclass of circuits.
definitions: exact-center regime: the forbidden ball centers range over every circuit of size at most 2^{epsilon m}.
debited-center regime: the forbidden centers range only over circuits of size at most 2^{(epsilon-rho)m}, and an edit list of size 2^{rho m} may be hardwired.
multiplexed target length: n is kappa(1+D)m up to lower-order padding terms.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Repairs the quantitative transfer invariant from cycle 54 by separating exact hardness extraction from sparse-edit robustness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The radius parameter rho should be charged only when the certificate excludes centers below 2^{(epsilon-rho)m}. If the anti-ball statement excludes all centers of size 2^{epsilon m}, exact MCSP extraction loses no rho; rho is then only robustness against sparse-edit implementations.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if every candidate binding mechanism either reduces to T-oracle transcript checking below 2^{epsilon m}/m, uses nonuniform advice, or becomes a dense constructive natural property.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if a uniform proof-complexity or algebraic commitment source proves UNSAT(Near_{m,2^{epsilon m},2^{rho m}}(T)) with low-D row generation, no advice, and an explicit argument that zero-fill replay is impossible.
control_decision.reason: The carrier transfer is quantitatively valid, but the remaining source cannot be a sparse black-box proof. The next viable object is a named non-black-box proof or commitment system that binds the entire truth table without advice and without becoming a large natural property.

dependency_updates.description: Exact anti-ball exclusion against centers of size 2^{epsilon m} supports delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)); the epsilon-rho loss is valid only in the debited-center or sparse-edit reconstruction regime.
Black-box symbolic source verifiers require transcript load Omega(2^{epsilon m}/m) or a non-black-box binding interface; otherwise zero-fill replay accepts an easy row.

Short O(m)-bit certificates remain E-friendly for enumeration but cannot be black-box anti-ball proofs at constant epsilon; exponential-load proofs need an explicit generator rather than brute-force canonicalization.
The zero-fill argument is relativizing for T-oracle verifiers. Any surviving source must be non-black-box and probably non-natural; merely invoking proof complexity is not enough.

falsifiers: Sparse T-query symbolic certificates with q=2^{theta m} for theta<epsilon are a falsifier for universal MCSP no-side soundness, by zero-fill replay.
A certificate proving anti-ball exclusion only for centers of size 2^{(epsilon-rho)m) but claiming delta near epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) fails the valid quantitative transfer test.
